# Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover

Day 3, 11:45 · Google · coverage: slides

Slides only: Discover eligibility, E-E-A-T and large image requirements. No recording; the presenter is not named on the photographed slides.

## Claims

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide showed an eligibility gate: content with a policy violation goes to a policy compliance check and low-quality content to an E-E-A-T quality check, and both can end with the content filtered out, while safe and trusted content becomes eligible for Discover.
  <br><sub>`D3-C218` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover), [Discover content policies](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/9982767?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Discover documentation says content is automatically eligible for Discover if it is indexed and meets Discover's content policies, needs no special tags or structured data, and is not guaranteed to appear.
  <br><sub>`D3-C219` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover · is the documentation · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by the glossary term *Google Discover*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Discover documentation says Discover uses many of the same signals and systems as Search to determine what is helpful, people-first content.
  <br><sub>`D3-C220` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover · is the documentation · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by the glossary term *Google Discover*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide said that for eligible content image quality decides click-through: a small thumbnail lowers the click-through rate and a large, high-resolution image raises it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C221` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide defined E-E-A-T: experience means first-hand, personal experience with the topic, expertise the necessary knowledge or skill, and authoritativeness the extent to which the creator or website is known as a go-to source for the topic.
  <br><sub>`D3-C222` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [General Guidelines](https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf), [Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) · Used by the glossary term *E-E-A-T*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide said trust comes first: untrustworthy pages have low E-E-A-T however experienced, expert or authoritative they seem.
  > "untrustworthy pages will have low E-E-A-T no matter how Experienced, Expert or Authoritative they may seem"
  <br><sub>`D3-C223` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [General Guidelines](https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf), [Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) · Used by the glossary term *E-E-A-T*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide recommended large images at least 1,200 px wide, with more than 300,000 total pixels and a 16x9 aspect ratio, enabled by the max-image-preview:large setting.
  <br><sub>`D3-C224` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Extends [D2-C089](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Repeats [D2-C936](D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-04`, `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide said to avoid generic images, such as a site logo, and text-heavy images.
  <br><sub>`D3-C225` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide said images are subject to the same policy requirements as the content and that misleading, exaggerated or outrageous images should be avoided.
  <br><sub>`D3-C226` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover), [Discover content policies](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/9982767?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Discover documentation says to specify the large image with schema.org markup or the og:image meta tag, which can influence the thumbnail Discover chooses, and that a vertical image cropped to 16x9 must keep its important details.
  <br><sub>`D3-C227` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover · is the documentation · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's closing Discover slide pointed to the Discover content policies in Google Search Help and to the Search Central documentation.
  <br><sub>`D3-C228` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Discover content policies ask news sources for clear dates and bylines, information about the authors, publication and publisher, and contact information, and say repeated or egregious violations can make a site ineligible for Discover.
  <br><sub>`D3-C229` · Google Search Help · annotates Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover · is the documentation · [Discover content policies](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/9982767?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For Discover, set max-image-preview:large on article templates, give every article a relevant image at least 1,200 px wide in og:image or schema.org markup that is neither the site logo nor text-heavy, and show clear bylines and dates.
  <br><sub>`D3-C230` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover), [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>
